title: Quality & Customer Service Adventure
welcome_lead: Great quality and friendly service keep customers coming back. ⭐
meta_desc: People & Operations Adventure 3 — KS3 Business Studies on quality control and customer service.
final_note: You learned why quality matters, how it's controlled, and what great service looks like.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Poor quality means returns, refunds and bad reviews.

Good quality keeps customers happy and protects the reputation. ⭐

Quality control — check items at the end of the line. Reject the bad ones.

Quality assurance — build quality in at every stage. Stop bad ones from being made in the first place.

Service is everything around the product:

  • Friendly staff.
  • Quick answers.
  • Fair returns.
  • Solving complaints quickly.

One bad experience can become a viral video. 📱

mcqs.q: Why might a business adopt corporate social responsibility (CSR)?
options: Reasons include genuine ethics, but also commercial benefits — improved reputation, customer loyalty, employee retention, and reduced regulatory or reputational risk.
Liquidity ratios measure how quickly a business sells products.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
CSR is purely about being ethical with no business benefit.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a mission statement?
options: To define the business's core purpose and values, guiding decisions and communicating identity to stakeholders — answering 'why we exist'.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
A mission statement is a description of what products the business sells.
A mission statement is a list of financial targets.

mcqs.q: What does a liquidity ratio like the current ratio measure?
options: Liquidity ratios measure how quickly a business sells products.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
A business's ability to meet short-term obligations — current assets divided by current liabilities. A ratio above 1 means assets cover liabilities; too high may indicate poor use of resources.
A higher liquidity ratio is always better.
